[
{"text":"Executing a person who deliberately kills an innocent victim is the only proportionate response to the gravity of that crime.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Life imprisonment is an inadequate punishment for mass murderers and serial killers who show no remorse.","side":"A"},
{"text":"The threat of execution deters some would-be murderers who would not be stopped by a prison sentence.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Families of murder victims deserve the closure that only the execution of the killer can provide.","side":"A"},
{"text":"A society that refuses to execute its worst offenders fails to express the true value it places on innocent life.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Executing a murderer permanently guarantees that the person can never kill again, inside prison or out.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Lethal injection delivers a humane death that is far gentler than the way murder victims die.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Modern DNA evidence has made wrongful convictions in capital cases rare enough to justify keeping the penalty.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Taxpayers should not be forced to feed and house child killers for the rest of their natural lives.","side":"A"},
{"text":"A murderer forfeits his own right to life by deliberately taking the life of another person.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Scripture's principle of a life for a life gives moral authority to the execution of murderers.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Prisoners serving life sentences with no hope of release have little reason not to attack guards and fellow inmates.","side":"A"},
{"text":"The prospect of a death sentence gives prosecutors leverage to obtain confessions and the locations of victims' bodies.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Retribution is a legitimate purpose of criminal law, and execution is its fullest expression for the worst crimes.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Juries sentencing a murderer to death are exercising democratic judgment that deserves respect rather than being overridden by abolitionists.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Terrorists who kill civilians should face execution as a statement that society will not tolerate such atrocities.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Executing killers is no more a violation of human dignity than imprisoning kidnappers, since both punish chosen wrongs.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Countries that carry out executions send a stronger message against violent crime than countries that have abolished them.","side":"A"},
{"text":"A life sentence can be reduced by parole boards or pardons, while execution ensures the sentence is carried out.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Some crimes are so monstrous that no punishment short of death can satisfy the demands of justice.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Every execution risks killing an innocent person, and that irreversible mistake can never be undone or compensated.","side":"B"},
{"text":"The state has no moral authority to take a human life, even the life of a convicted murderer.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Studies comparing states and countries show no reliable evidence that executions reduce homicide rates more than imprisonment does.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Capital cases cost taxpayers far more than life imprisonment because of lengthy trials and mandatory appeals.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Defendants who are poor or belong to racial minorities are far more likely to receive a death sentence for similar crimes.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Life without parole protects the public just as effectively as execution while leaving room to correct mistakes.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Killing a prisoner who is already helpless is revenge dressed up as justice, and it lowers the state to the killer's level.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Botched lethal injections have caused prolonged agony, showing that no method of execution is reliably humane.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Every person retains an inherent right to life that no crime and no government can legitimately remove.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Executions prolong the grief of victims' families by dragging them through decades of appeals and media attention.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Religious teachings on mercy and redemption forbid the state from putting a repentant sinner to death.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Dozens of death row inmates have been exonerated, proving that the justice system convicts innocent people of capital crimes.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Most developed democracies have abolished capital punishment, which marks it as a relic of a less civilized age.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Prison staff and doctors forced to take part in executions suffer lasting psychological harm.","side":"B"},
{"text":"A government that kills its own citizens as punishment teaches the public that killing is an acceptable solution to problems.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Murderers who spend their lives in prison can reflect, repent, and sometimes contribute to the lives of others.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Prosecutors and juries apply the death penalty arbitrarily, so who is executed depends more on geography and luck than on guilt.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Condemned inmates endure years of dread on death row, a form of psychological torture that amounts to cruel punishment.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Money spent on executions would do more good if directed toward crime prevention and support for victims' families.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Abolishing the death penalty reflects moral progress, as societies have gradually rejected torture, mutilation, and public killings.","side":"B"}
]
